minutes.headline: PACC discussed the failed Jan 17 high school auditorium broadcast and reviewed a draft FY24 budget; a warrant article and drone policy were moved.
minutes.summary: The Public Access Cable Committee spent most of the meeting on a postmortem of the January 17 town meeting live stream from the high school auditorium, where the encoder froze and audio was poor, and on who is responsible for the school's audio board, network and feed. It then walked through the draft FY24 budget spreadsheet, adjusting no lines finally, and went through the annual town report draft. The committee moved the minutes, a warrant article and a drone policy, and discussed moving the next meeting date.

what_happened.line: The Public Access Cable Committee spent most of the meeting on why the January 17 town meeting live stream from the high school auditorium failed.
The committee moved to send a warrant article funding the FY24 PEG access operating and capital budgets; the outcome was not audible in the recording.
The committee reviewed a draft FY24 budget line by line but did not vote it; members are to send questions and finish at the next meeting.
A motion to adopt the drone policy language as read was made; the outcome was not audible in the recording.
The manager is to meet town and IT staff this week about the auditorium feed, and the committee wants the audio-feed boundary clarified.

why_it_matters: The warrant article funds public access cable operations and equipment, so residents may be asked to vote on it at town meeting, and the recording does not show whether the committee approved sending it.
The unsettled question of who runs the school's audio board, network and feed bears on whether live broadcasts from the auditorium work at the next town meeting.
watch_next: The next meeting, March 6, where the committee is to finish the FY24 budget; a move to the second Monday of the month depends on room availability.
The outcome of the manager's meeting with town and IT staff about the auditorium feed.
